nodes.description: A subgroup has severe, disabling chronic flank or loin pain, usually with very high stone activity but sometimes without obstruction or an identifiable stone; many need daily opioids.

evidence.reference_title: Chronic pain in medullary sponge kidney: a rare and never described clinical presentation.
evidence.snippet: 71% of participants referred a daily pain that interfered strongly with everyday life and quality of life (WQL mean value 29.4)

evidence.reference_title: Medullary sponge kidney and chronic pain: is there a role for renal denervation.
evidence.snippet: It commonly presents with recurrent calcium nephrolithiasis and often, severe, life-altering chronic pain syndromes, often independent of urinary obstruction and of uncertain etiology.

nodes.description: Proposed developmental origin. Rare heterozygous GDNF regulatory variants were found in some patients and cosegregated with MSK in families, and MSK co-occurs with extrarenal anomalies of tissues that also depend on GDNF-RET signaling. A later exome study of 42 patients, with a screen of a larger variant datastore, found no GDNF, RET or GFRA1 association, so this is at most a cause in a subset of patients.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of GDNF gene sequence variations in patients with medullary sponge kidney disease.
evidence.snippet: Five of the eight cases were found to be familial, and the allele variants cosegregated with the disease in a seemingly dominant pattern of inheritance.

evidence.reference_title: New non-renal congenital disorders associated with medullary sponge kidney (MSK) support the pathogenic role of GDNF and point to the diagnosis of MSK in recurrent stone formers.
evidence.snippet: The discovery of disorders involving the central nervous system, cardiovascular system and craniofacial skeleton in MSK patients supports the hypothesis of a genetic alteration on the RET-GDNF axis having a pivotal role in the pathogenesis of MSK, in a subset of patients at least.

evidence.reference_title: Exome sequencing in patients with medullary sponge kidney.
evidence.snippet: A total of 140 rare variants of RET (n = 107), GDNF (n = 11) and GFR α1 (n = 22) were identified in the variant datastore, none was associated with MSK.

nodes.description: Usually incomplete, unmasked by ammonium chloride loading. Reported frequency varies widely between series (8 of 13 in one, none of 12 biopsy-proven cases in another).

evidence.reference_title: Renal acidification defects in medullary sponge kidney.
evidence.snippet: Nine patients had some form of renal acidification defect; 8 had the distal type of renal tubular acidosis, 2 the complete and 6 the incomplete form.

nodes.description: Many patients have incomplete (or occasionally complete) distal renal tubular acidosis on ammonium chloride loading, with higher fasting urine pH, hypocitraturia and hypercalciuria, attributed to secondary collecting duct dysfunction. The defect is not found in every series.

evidence.reference_title: Biopsy proven medullary sponge kidney: clinical findings, histopathology, and role of osteogenesis in stone and plaque formation.
evidence.snippet: Patients had no abnormalities of urinary acidification or acid excretion; the most frequent metabolic abnormality was idiopathic hypercalciuria.

evidence.snippet: A case-control study revealed that these two alleles were significantly associated with MSK.

evidence.snippet: Four patients had incomplete renal tubular acidiosis (iRTA), 3 had hypercalciuria, and 5 patients had hypocitraturia.

evidence.snippet: quite frequently had also reduced citraturia (64% in the whole population)

nodes.description: The defining lesion: enlarged, billowy papillae with markedly dilated inner medullary collecting ducts forming 1-8 mm cysts, often containing small mobile ductal stones, sometimes with dilated ducts of Bellini. Bilateral in about 70% of cases; may be segmental.

evidence.reference_title: Biopsy proven medullary sponge kidney: clinical findings, histopathology, and role of osteogenesis in stone and plaque formation.
evidence.snippet: Affected papillae are enlarged and billowy, due to markedly enlarged inner medullary collecting ducts (IMCD), which contain small, mobile ductal stones.

evidence.reference_title: Spontaneous calcification process in primary renal cells from a medullary sponge kidney patient harbouring a GDNF mutation.
evidence.snippet: Medullary nephrocalcinosis is a hallmark of medullary sponge kidney (MSK).

nodes.description: The cystic dilatations of the medullary collecting ducts that give the kidney its sponge-like appearance; 1 to 8 mm in diameter.

evidence.reference_title: Medullary Sponge Kidney.
evidence.snippet: These numerous small cysts range in diameter from 1 to 8 millimeters and give the kidney, when cut, the appearance of a sponge, thus the name.

nodes.description: Recurrent calcium oxalate and apatite stones, the main clinical presentation, typically from the third decade. Most clinical cohorts are recruited from stone formers, so no unbiased frequency is available.

evidence.reference_title: Medullary sponge kidney: state of the art.
evidence.snippet: Medullary sponge kidney (MSK) is a kidney malformation that generally manifests with nephrocalcinosis and recurrent renal stones

nodes.description: Papillary cells cultured from a GDNF-variant MSK patient calcified spontaneously and expressed osteoblastic markers, and GDNF knockdown in renal tubular cells promoted calcium phosphate deposition. In biopsy-proven cases, osteogenic transcription factors were expressed in papillae without mineral at those sites, arguing against this route.

evidence.reference_title: Spontaneous calcification process in primary renal cells from a medullary sponge kidney patient harbouring a GDNF mutation.
evidence.snippet: In addition, the MSK cells expressed osteocalcin and osteonectin, indicating an osteoblast-like phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: Biopsy proven medullary sponge kidney: clinical findings, histopathology, and role of osteogenesis in stone and plaque formation.
evidence.snippet: Although both Runx2 and Osterix are expressed in papillae of MSK patients, no mineral deposition was seen at the sites of gene expression, arguing against a role of these genes in this process.

nodes.description: Long-term oral potassium citrate raises urinary citrate and pH, lowers urinary calcium, markedly reduces stone recurrence and improves bone density in MSK patients with urinary stone risk factors. Evidence is from observational cohorts, not randomized trials.

evidence.reference_title: Long-term treatment with potassium citrate and renal stones in medullary sponge kidney.
evidence.snippet: KC led to a dramatic reduction in the stone event rate (from 0.58 to 0.10 stones/yr per patient)

evidence.reference_title: Bone disease in medullary sponge kidney and effect of potassium citrate treatment.
evidence.snippet: Bone density improved significantly in the group that was treated with oral CA.

evidence.reference_title: Medullary Sponge Kidney.
evidence.snippet: It is usually asymptomatic but can present with hematuria, urinary tract infections (UTIs), or renal stone formation.

nodes.description: Frequent in patients with MSK and urinary stone risk factors; improves with long-term potassium citrate.

evidence.reference_title: Bone disease in medullary sponge kidney and effect of potassium citrate treatment.
evidence.snippet: Bone disease is very frequent in patients with MSK and concomitant PSRF.

evidence.reference_title: Bone disease in medullary sponge kidney and effect of potassium citrate treatment.
evidence.snippet: 59% had a T score between −1.0 and −2.5 (osteopenia) and 12% had <−2.5 (osteoporosis)

nodes.description: Lithotripsy or surgical removal of symptomatic stones, reserved for recurrent stones with severe symptoms.

evidence.reference_title: Medullary Sponge Kidney: Current Perspectives.
evidence.snippet: As a last line choice, surgical intervention including the removal of stones may be a choice for patients who experience both recurrent stone formation and harsh clinical symptoms.

nodes.description: Thiazides reduce urinary calcium and are used alongside or instead of potassium citrate to prevent calcium stones; no trial has tested them specifically in MSK.

evidence.reference_title: Medullary Sponge Kidney: Current Perspectives.
evidence.snippet: Thiazide diuretics can be added as an adjunctive measure to decrease rates of calcium stone formation in the distal nephron.

evidence.reference_title: Long-term treatment with potassium citrate and renal stones in medullary sponge kidney.
evidence.snippet: With reference to the prevention of renal stones in patients with MSK, thiazides and KC are suggested (6), although no trial has formally studied their usefulness.

nodes.description: Slow urine flow through the dilated ducts favors crystallization of calcium oxalate and apatite; ductal stones pass into the pelvis and seed larger stones. This mechanism does not require a metabolic abnormality.

evidence.reference_title: Biopsy proven medullary sponge kidney: clinical findings, histopathology, and role of osteogenesis in stone and plaque formation.
evidence.snippet: Stones may form over white (Randall's) plaque, but most renal pelvic stones are not attached, and have a similar morphology as ductal stones, which are a mixture of calcium oxalate and apatite.
